title: Fruits Into Baskets II
summary: Given two arrays, fruits and baskets, each of length n, place each fruit type in the leftmost available basket with sufficient capacity, ensuring each basket holds only one type of fruit.
statement: Given two arrays, fruits and baskets, each of length n, place each fruit type in the leftmost available basket with sufficient capacity, ensuring each basket holds only one type of fruit. If a fruit type cannot be placed, it remains unplaced. Return the count of unplaced fruit types.
constraints: Process fruit quantities from left to right.
Place each in the leftmost unused basket whose capacity is at least that quantity.
Return how many fruit types cannot be placed.
hints: Maintain whether each basket remains unused.
For each fruit, scan baskets from the left.
Consume the first unused basket with sufficient capacity; otherwise increment the unplaced count.
This direct simulation enforces both processing and leftmost-choice order.
editorial: This direct simulation enforces both processing and leftmost-choice order.

tests.explanation: Four uses capacity five, two uses capacity three, and five has no remaining fit, so one is unplaced.
Each fruit fits the leftmost remaining basket, so none is unplaced.
